title: W01. A gcd–lcm process
source: **Source:** IMO 2026, Problem 1; [official paper](https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2026/2026_eng.pdf). Mixed number theory and combinatorics.
statement: Begin with 2026 integers greater than one. A move chooses two current entries \(a,b>1\) and replaces them by \(g=\gcd(a,b)\) and \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)/g\). Prove that play must end with exactly one entry greater than one, and that this final entry is independent of all choices.

title: W02. Two covering counts have the same parity
statement: In a finite bipartite acquaintance graph with parts \(L,R\), a subset of either part covers the other part when every vertex of the other part has a neighbor in it. Prove that the numbers of covering subsets on the two sides have the same parity.

title: W03. Edges above the bipartite threshold force triangles
statement:
A simple graph has \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges. Prove that its number \(t\) of triangles satisfies
\[
t\ge\frac{4m(m-n^2/4)}{3n}.
\]

title: W04. One illuminated square
statement: On a \(5\times5\) board, a switch toggles its own light and its orthogonally adjacent lights. Starting with all lights off, which positions can be the only illuminated square?

title: W05. An odd grid and a saturated count
statement: Color each edge of an \(n\times n\) grid red or blue, where \(n\) is odd. If at most \(n^2\) edges are red, prove that a unit square has at least three blue edges.

title: W06. An odd route with distinct airlines
statement: An \(n\)-vertex flight network has \(n\) airline colors. Each color supports an odd closed route. Prove that an odd closed route exists whose edges have pairwise different colors.

title: W07. A convex-hull identity
statement:
Let \(S\) be a finite planar set with no three collinear points. For a convex polygon \(P\) with vertices in \(S\), let \(a(P)\) count its vertices and \(b(P)\) the points of \(S\) outside it. Include segments, points and the empty polygon. Prove for every real \(x\) that
\[
\sum_P x^{a(P)}(1-x)^{b(P)}=1.
\]

title: W08. Tournaments generated by commuting involutions
statement: In each of \(k\) rounds, \(n\) players are paired, with no pair repeated. Require that whenever \(A,B\) and \(C,D\) are pairs in one round and \(A,C\) is a pair in another, then \(B,D\) is also a pair in that other round. Determine the possible positive integers \((n,k)\).

title: W09. Synchronized bishops
statement: Put one labeled bishop in each square of the top row of a \(2^n\times2^n\) board. A jump moves every bishop diagonally so that they again occupy distinct squares in one common row. How many orders can occur on the bottom row?

title: W10. Preventing a directed cycle forever
statement: Ann and Bob alternately orient previously unoriented unit edges of the infinite square grid, with Ann first. Bob wins if a directed cycle ever appears, including after Ann's move. Can he force a win?

title: W11. A sum-free sequence at the density boundary
source: **Source:** USA TSTST 2013, Problem 1, as identified in the recovered selection booklet. **Record:** `usa_2013_bfa49c`.
statement: Find all strictly increasing positive integer sequences \((a_i)\) with no equation \(a_i+a_j=a_k\), allowing repeated indices, and with \(a_k=2k-1\) for infinitely many \(k\).

title: W12. Large disjoint cross-intersecting families
statement: For every \(0<\alpha<(3-\sqrt5)/2\), find \(n,p\) with \(p>\alpha2^n\) and two disjoint families \(\mathcal S,\mathcal T\), each of \(p\) distinct subsets of \([n]\), such that each member of \(\mathcal S\) intersects every member of \(\mathcal T\).

title: W13. Fifteen subsets of a 56-element set
source: **Source:** China Mathematical Olympiad 2006, Problem 6, attributed to Leng Gangsong. **Record:** `chn_2006_c22bc5`.
statement: Find the smallest integer \(N\) such that, if every seven of fifteen subsets of a 56-element set have union of size at least \(N\), some three subsets have a common element.

title: W14. Forcing a rainbow three-cell window
statement: An \(n\times n\) board, \(n\ge3\), uses exactly \(C=\lfloor(n+2)^2/3\rfloor\) colors. Prove that some horizontal or vertical three-cell window has three different colors.

title: W15. The anti-Pascal pyramid
source: **Source:** IMO 2018, Problem 3; also IMO Shortlist 2018, C4. **Record:** `imo_2018_55614a`.
statement: In a triangular array, every entry above the bottom row equals the absolute difference of its two children. Can an array with 2018 rows contain every integer from 1 through \(1+2+\cdots+2018\) exactly once?

title: W16. Knights against blocking queens
statement: Horst places a knight on an empty square of a \(20\times20\) board without attacking any previous knight. Queenie then occupies an empty square with a queen. They repeat until a player cannot move. Queens only occupy squares; they impose no attack restriction. What number of knights can Horst guarantee?

title: W17. One spanning tree meeting three quotas
statement: A connected graph has \(r+g+b+1\) vertices, with red, green and blue edges. There is a spanning tree with exactly \(r\) red edges, another with exactly \(g\) green edges, and another with exactly \(b\) blue edges. Prove that one tree meets all three quotas simultaneously.

title: W18. Keeping 150 entries of a doubly stochastic matrix
source: **Source:** China TST 2023, Test Three, Day 2, Problem 6. **Record:** `chn_2023_a44cf5`.
statement: In any nonnegative \(100\times100\) matrix with every row sum and column sum equal to one, retain 150 entries and set the others to zero. What is the largest universal lower bound \(\lambda\) on all remaining row and column sums?

title: W19. A set whose largest half is constrained
statement: For a positive integer \(k\), find the least \(N\) for which \(2k+1\) distinct positive integers have total sum greater than \(N\), while every \(k\)-element subset has sum at most \(N/2\).

title: W20. Unique subsums with odd parts
statement: A partition of 9999 into odd positive parts is called sum-friendly if each integer from 0 to 9999 has exactly one subsum representation. Equal copies of a part are indistinguishable: a representation specifies only how many copies of each distinct value are used. Count the sum-friendly partitions.

title: W21. Equal totals but strongly unbalanced rows and columns
statement: An \(m\times n\) board contains equal numbers of two symbols. In each row their counts differ by at least \(n/2\), and in each column by at least \(m/2\). Show that \(m,n\) are divisible by four, and construct such a board for \(m=n=2016\).

title: W22. Cookie pebbling on an even cycle
source: **Source:** Korean Mathematical Olympiad 2010, Problem 5. National pipeline supplement. **Record:** `kor_2010_1dc4be`.
statement: At the vertices of a cycle with \(2n\) vertices are nonnegative integer numbers of cookies. A move consumes two cookies at a vertex and places one at a neighboring vertex. Find the smallest total number guaranteeing that a prescribed vertex can obtain a cookie, regardless of the initial distribution.

title: W23. A finite state space with draws
statement: Starting from positive piles \((a,b)\), Alice and Bob alternate, Alice first. A move chooses an even pile and transfers half of it to the other pile. A player with no legal move loses. Determine exactly when Bob can force a win.

title: W24. The fewest tiles in a maximal placement
statement: Let \(k\ge2\) and \(k\le n\le2k-1\). Place nonoverlapping \(1\times k\) or \(k\times1\) tiles on an \(n\times n\) board until no further tile fits. What is the smallest possible number of tiles?

title: W25. A private witness in every proper-union subfamily
statement: Let \(|X|=n>1\). A family of distinct proper nonempty subsets of \(X\) has the following property: every nonempty subfamily whose union is not \(X\) has an element belonging to exactly one member of that subfamily. Find its maximum size.

title: W26. Reducing a set by sum-and-difference moves
statement: Start with \(\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\), \(n\ge2\). Erase two distinct current numbers \(a,b\), and insert \(a+b\) and \(|a-b|\), suppressing any duplicate with an existing number. Can the set be reduced to exactly two elements?
